short_description: Adult ADHD telehealth service (Abe Health LLC) that shut down in 2022; no longer available.
long_description: Ahead (legally Abe Health LLC) was a US telehealth startup that diagnosed and treated adult ADHD by video, with salaried clinicians and 60-minute first visits. Its main investor, Truepill, had put about $9 million into the company before shifting to business-to-business services. Ahead stopped accepting new patients in mid-April 2022 and planned to end care for current patients by June 24, 2022. Its website, helloahead.com, now shows only a maintenance page.

pricing.notes: Service closed in 2022; no current pricing.

privacy.notes: Service closed in 2022; its privacy policy is no longer online.

seo.meta_description: AHEAD provides online ADHD treatment with licensed psychiatrists and therapists, offering personalized medication management and support.

faqs.a: AHEAD accepts most major insurance plans. For self-pay, expect $200-300/month for medication management. Therapy sessions are additional. Contact them for current pricing as it varies by service and location.

AHEAD psychiatrists can prescribe ADHD medications including stimulants when clinically appropriate. Your provider will work with you to find the right medication and dosage based on your needs and medical history.

faqs.q: What makes AHEAD different from other ADHD platforms?
faqs.a: AHEAD specializes exclusively in ADHD, with providers who understand the condition deeply. They offer both medication management and therapy, recognizing ADHD affects multiple life areas. The focused approach may benefit those wanting specialized care.

faqs.q: How quickly can I get an appointment with AHEAD?
faqs.a: Most patients can schedule initial appointments within 1-2 weeks. Wait times vary by location and provider availability. The platform works to minimize waiting as ADHD treatment timing matters.

availability.note: Stopped taking new patients in April 2022 and ended care for existing patients by June 24, 2022.

patient_summary: Ahead was an online ADHD clinic for adults that offered video visits with psychiatric clinicians. It stopped taking new patients in April 2022 and ended care for existing patients that June, so you can't sign up. If you're looking for ADHD care, a psychiatrist, your primary care doctor, or another telehealth ADHD service is the place to start.
